approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from the original unlabeled corpus strings and retains the checkpoint with the lowest heldout token loss. Each objective clones that prior into an adaptable flow policy and keeps the reference prior frozen. The online loop alternates a neural batch with two graph batches; accepted neural molecules refresh the breeding population and provide a protected parent at the first graph handoff. Accepted-score fingerprint posterior samples choose the other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance learning of the neural policy. The same reciprocal loop is retained here. The preparation choice being questioned is its use of string likelihood alone to decide which learned prior all those components receive.
approach.novelty: Choose the prepared checkpoint by its observed yield of valid, connected, distinct molecules under a fixed ancestral sampling probe, with heldout token loss breaking ties. A separate diagnostic probe then compares that choice with the ordinary loss-minimizing checkpoint from the same training trajectory. This sibling changes checkpoint selection, whereas the previous preparation sibling changed the strings used for training. It neither combines the two interventions nor changes neural learning, graph construction or posterior allocation during an objective.

hypothesis: Select the reusable prior checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid-connected-unique molecular emission yield among unlabeled checkpoints that improve the initial holdout loss, breaking ties by lower original-string holdout NLL while preserving the Parent training and stopping rules.

finding_summary.headline: Checkpoint selection raises endpoint scores, while molecular-yield gains transfer unevenly
finding_summary.insights:
The minimum token-loss checkpoint is not the only useful prior along the same unchanged learning trajectory. This experiment cleanly separates checkpoint choice from changes to training representations, gradients or the online search algorithm. It also exposes the limitation of the selection criterion: choosing among 60 checkpoints with one fixed 256-draw sample creates a selection-sample advantage that mostly disappears on fresh diagnostic randomness in two seeds. That pattern is compatible with selection noise and supports only limited generalization of the measured yield gain. The lower online raw validity shows that valid prior sampling and useful adaptation should remain separate measurements; even the first online batch follows accepted-score policy updates.

The molecular assessment gives the same distinction a chemical interpretation. Useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements coexist with unusual sulfur bonding, nitroso groups, peroxide bonds and unresolved stereochemistry. Valid connected uniqueness does not distinguish those liabilities, and higher endpoint scores do not establish better synthetic plausibility. The campaign now has evidence that an earlier checkpoint can improve the reciprocal search without a reliably better valid-emission rate. Whether a more representative unlabeled diagnostic can predict that downstream usefulness remains open.
finding_summary.results:
The rule selected different prior weights in all three preparations. On the fixed selection samples, the chosen checkpoints produced 243, 245 and 238 valid, distinct molecules out of 256, compared with 232, 236 and 229 for the lowest-loss checkpoints from the same training trajectories. The independent diagnostic changed those counts by -1, +10 and 0; its pooled gain was only 9 of 768 draws, compared with 29 of 768 on the selection samples. Thus checkpoint choice and its selection-sample advantage are established, while an independent yield advantage appeared in only one seed. All training runs completed the same 29,742 updates, and the ordinary lowest-loss weights exactly matched the published parent weights, so no training-length difference explains the choice. The selected checkpoints incurred small token-loss increases of 0.001852, 0.002624 and 0.003124.

During optimization, valid terminated neural draws fell from 8,441 of 12,000 to 8,156 of 12,000, or 70.34% to 67.97%. Nevertheless, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.520669 to 0.550198, with paired gains of 0.026285, 0.051553 and 0.010747. The mean gain, 0.029528, exceeds the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin task means improved; zaleplon was nearly unchanged and DRD2 declined slightly. Every task completed the supplied evaluation panel. The new checkpoints therefore changed useful downstream search outcomes, but the score increase cannot be explained as a consistent increase in valid molecular emission.

molecular.headline: Rich aryl, amine and carbonyl rings coexist with triple-bonded sulfur, nitroso groups, peroxides and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All 4,500 child trajectory rows and 4,500 corresponding Parent rows were read, including 4,350 optimizer proposals in each node. Each task supplies 900 evaluated molecules, of which 870 are optimizer proposals. The child has abundant fused heteroaromatics, saturated amine rings, aryl amides, sulfonamides and carbonyl heterocycles. Its ring-closure marker rates are 0.9816–0.9943; aromatic-marker rates are 0.7736–0.9747, with the lower value reflecting substantial unsaturated nonaromatic ring chemistry in one output set. These digest counters measure string-level presence, not atom fractions or perceived ring quality. Read-only RDKit inspection parses all 4,350 emitted child SMILES and gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 in the supplied task order. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures coexist with unusually bonded sulfur, N-nitroso substituents, peroxide bonds, highly contracted unsaturated rings and oversized assemblies. All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 392, 225, 563, 348 and 353 optimizer rows respectively, with assigned centres in none. The repertoire varies across seeds, while the upper tails repeatedly revisit a few related families. Chemistry quality is therefore mixed: ring and aromatic content are rich, but neither parseability nor high observed scores establish synthetic accessibility, stability or well-defined geometry. This assessment describes the output without attributing it to an algorithmic mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The digest leaders are medium-sized heteroaryl structures. Seed 0 links a quinoline-like ring system to a fused five/five-membered aza-ring framework; its leading variants carry N–O or N–O–N attachments and an oxygen-linked carbon triply bonded to hydrogen-bearing sulfur. The leading molecule has 25 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, three aromatic. Seed 2 also provides a more conventional methoxy/cyano-substituted partially saturated quinoline-like carboxamide and a different hydroxy-nitrile/amidine series with unsaturated carbocyclic or oxygen-containing rings. Across the full optimizer output the median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings, as in the Parent. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 577 for the child and 529 for the Parent; this counts local ring edits as distinct and is not a count of useful synthetic series. The Parent leaders included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide, indole-amide and quinoline/urea families. Rings, nitrogen and carbonyl groups are thus not missing, but the new leading families include more problematic connectivity.
liabilities: Fifty-one of 870 child proposals contain a carbon–sulfur triple bond, versus none in the corresponding Parent task. The leading C≡S–H environment and N–O–N or O–S attachments are not ordinary medicinal functional groups, and parsing supplies no stability or synthetic evidence.

The hydroxy-nitrile and unsaturated ring families include potentially sensitive local connectivity and unassigned stereocentres. Relative stability and geometry of those proposed forms are not established by the trajectory.
Ten optimizer proposals have at most three heavy atoms. Such fragments, as well as the cited large polyfunctional assembly, lose the connected arrangement seen in the favorable examples.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that preserve the favorable local aryl/nitrogen/substituent arrangement are not consistently established within the sulfur-rich leading family. A separate conventional nitrile/amide family is present, so the limitation is not an inability to make amides or nitriles.
Defined configurations are absent for substituted fused-ring and hydroxy-nitrile centres. The data do not establish which stereoisomer, if any, would be preferred.
Controlled core replacements preserving useful local functionality remain incomplete: some changes retain the core but sharply lose the score, while fragmentation removes it entirely.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The oxygen-linked C≡S–H structure with an N–O–N substituent scores 0.49151859442707624; the corresponding O–S substituent gives 0.46889981462810426, while the N–O version retaining C≡S–H gives 0.4509940583060807. A methoxy/N-hydroxy relative scores 0.4524187090179798. These observations show that questionable bonding is accepted among the favorable local variants, not that the sulfur motif is chemically necessary. The cyano/carboxamide alternative scores 0.46457806514522626; replacing its nitrile by methyl gives 0.31305283559478153, N-methylating its amide gives 0.4098058836024565, and replacing a methyl substituent by amino gives 0.3487840659540038. Those close-family comparisons associate the score with specific nitrile, amide and substitution relationships. The hydroxy-nitrile/amidine family reaches 0.4572645941803378. Sulfur, hydrazine, methane, a saturated sulfur-rich bicyclic structure and a large polyol/amide assembly all appear at 0.0. The pooled median is 0.177987. No uniquely required absent heterocycle follows from these whole-molecule observations.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail is dominated by a seed-1 diaryl-ether assembly with two quinazoline-like fused aza-aromatic systems, an N-acetylpiperazinone and a carbamoyl side chain often containing sulfur and an N-nitroso group. The leader has 45 heavy atoms and five six-membered rings, four aromatic. Related high examples substitute other heteroaromatic/sulfonamide connections around the same piperazinone-bearing aza-aromatic motif. These contain recognizable building blocks but combine substantial size with sensitive terminal chemistry. Other seeds explore sulfonamides with peroxide-containing side chains and aminoalkyl heteroaromatics with anionic N–O groups. The child median is 36 heavy atoms and four rings, matching the Parent medians, but 185 of 870 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals. The digest mean SMILES length is 70.4 and charged-marker rate is 0.2356. Parent leaders used other amino/imine/acylhydrazone-linked heteroaromatics; the new high family is a different, larger arrangement rather than evidence of generally absent heteroaromatic chemistry.
liabilities: The full child set contains N–N=O connectivity in 18 of 870 optimizer proposals, versus none in the corresponding Parent task; leading examples directly exhibit that group and sometimes an additional S–N linkage.

Read-only bond counts find O–O single bonds in 135 of 870 child proposals versus five Parent proposals, and O–halogen bonds in 93 versus seven. These are structural flags requiring chemical context, not measured reaction rates or an assertion that every flagged molecule is impossible.
Large, heteroatom-rich linked assemblies and anionic N–O variants complicate synthesis and physical-property interpretation. The supplied score does not establish those properties.
missing_features: Consistently credible terminal-group alternatives preserving the useful aza-aromatic/cyclic-carbonyl arrangement remain incomplete. A favorable score is shared by nitroso, thione, N-halogenated and more conventional variants, so none of those liabilities can be inferred to be a required feature.

Independent core/linker alternatives and controlled size reduction around the useful arrangement are not established as a systematic series. Much of the high tail changes peripheral decoration on related large assemblies.
Defined geometry and stereochemistry of the more complex saturated or fused variants are absent; the current observations do not identify an objective-preferred configuration.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are arylpiperazines joined by long carbon chains to an N-aryl five-membered nitrogen heterocycle or another aromatic group. Bromine, chlorine, fluorine, phenol and thiol substitutions recur. The leading structure has 32 heavy atoms and four rings, three aromatic, with a six-carbon linker to the piperazine; a simpler high example is a fluorophenylpiperazine with a five-carbon linker to phenyl. The Parent also produced arylpiperidines, aminoalkyl chains and fused saturated amines, so the broad accessible-amine/aromatic pattern is retained while the leading scaffold and linker choices change. Thiol-bearing or newly fused variants introduce additional chemical or geometric questions; favorable scores alone do not show oxidation stability or synthetic accessibility.

Core and linker changes that preserve the favorable arrangement without duplicating whole large fragments are incompletely controlled.

transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group edits do not consistently preserve chemically credible bonding around otherwise useful molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically coherent alternatives available while retaining the useful surrounding aromatic and polar relationships. Distinguish ordinary amide, amine, sulfur oxidation-state and carbon-bound-halogen changes from peroxide formation, nitrosation, unusual sulfur multiple bonding or heteroatom halogenation. Preserve chemical context rather than treating every parser-valid replacement as an equivalent functional group; let accepted feedback compare the actual alternatives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Full-trajectory RDKit checks find unassigned tetrahedral centres in 392, 225, 563, 348 and 353 optimizer rows in the brief task order and none assigned. The cited output includes substituted fused rings, hydroxy-nitrile centres, bridged amines and acetal-like linked rings; one high sulfur-containing family also contracts an unsaturated carbon ring to four members.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemical specification and controlled ring geometry remain absent or inconsistent in configurationally rich output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support specified configurations and chemically credible ring closure, expansion and contraction around accepted arrangements. Keep stereochemical, saturation and ring-size changes distinguishable so their consequences can be learned from current-session feedback. Missing specification alone does not establish a benefit for any particular stereoisomer or ring geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited zero-score molecules include methane, hydrazine, small nitrile-derived fragments, a long acyclic polyamine and oversized polyol/phosphate or polyene assemblies. A duplicated large aryl/amine structure gives 0.046770493414912545 despite near-limit scores for simpler members of that family. Conversely, a compact 32-heavy-atom diazepinone-containing structure scores 0.26493557493264663, and some larger linked heteroaromatics are themselves favorable. These observations support context-dependent size requirements, not a universal small-molecule rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size-changing moves sometimes destroy the useful connected arrangement through fragmentation or multiplication of whole motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore growth, contraction and linker alternatives that preserve a coherent core and useful local donor, acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships. Avoid relying mainly on tiny fragments or concatenating whole previously favorable structures, and let the current accepted observations determine useful molecular scale.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The upper excerpts repeatedly decorate a fused aza-ring family, linked quinazoline-like/piperazinone systems, long-linker arylpiperazines, lactam/sulfonylpiperazine cores and compact nitrogen/oxygen or sulfur-containing families. Different seeds demonstrate alternative chemistry, yet the full child nonchiral Murcko counts of 577, 692, 605, 684 and 532 also include small ring edits and large assemblies. Unique graphs therefore do not by themselves establish useful core coverage. Within a conventional nitrile/amide family, replacing nitrile with methyl changes the observed score from 0.46457806514522626 to 0.31305283559478153, illustrating the importance of local placement as well as core identity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically distinct useful cores and their functional-group arrangements receive uneven coverage within each leading neighborhood.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted core families and enable core or linker replacements that preserve useful functional-group placement and electronic context. Evaluate diversity through core chemistry and attachment relationships rather than only new strings, peripheral decorations or additional ring closures. Preserve the distinction between accessible amine, amide nitrogen, ring nitrogen and other polar environments while exploring alternatives.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

activation_observables.measurement: Per preparation seed, independently classify each logged raw selection-probe string with the unchanged Parent molecular checks and canonical identity. Reconstruct all eligible checkpoints and the lexicographic valid-unique-count/NLL/earliest-step selector. Compare its selected checkpoint with the original-NLL checkpoint from the identical training trajectory: report both steps and parameter identities, selection-probe raw/terminated/valid/unique/duplicate counts, valid-unique yield and signed difference. Report whether the rule actually selected different weights; a tie selecting the same weights supplies no changed-checkpoint activation. Verify the private purpose-tagged probe seed and reset behavior from code and receipts and that training RNGs remain untouched. On the independent final diagnostic stream report the same paired yields for both checkpoints, without using these results to select or rerun anything. A strict selection-panel gain establishes the intended allocation effect, whereas an independent-panel gain supports transfer beyond the selection sample. finding_summary.headline: Checkpoint selection raises endpoint scores, while molecular-yield gains transfer unevenly
finding_summary.insights:
The minimum token-loss checkpoint is not the only useful prior along the same unchanged learning trajectory. This experiment cleanly separates checkpoint choice from changes to training representations, gradients or the online search algorithm. It also exposes the limitation of the selection criterion: choosing among 60 checkpoints with one fixed 256-draw sample creates a selection-sample advantage that mostly disappears on fresh diagnostic randomness in two seeds. That pattern is compatible with selection noise and supports only limited generalization of the measured yield gain. The lower online raw validity shows that valid prior sampling and useful adaptation should remain separate measurements; even the first online batch follows accepted-score policy updates.

The molecular assessment gives the same distinction a chemical interpretation. Useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements coexist with unusual sulfur bonding, nitroso groups, peroxide bonds and unresolved stereochemistry. Valid connected uniqueness does not distinguish those liabilities, and higher endpoint scores do not establish better synthetic plausibility. The campaign now has evidence that an earlier checkpoint can improve the reciprocal search without a reliably better valid-emission rate. Whether a more representative unlabeled diagnostic can predict that downstream usefulness remains open.

This experiment cleanly separates checkpoint choice from changes to training representations, gradients or the online search algorithm. It also exposes the limitation of the selection criterion: choosing among 60 checkpoints with one fixed 256-draw sample creates a selection-sample advantage that mostly disappears on fresh diagnostic randomness in two seeds. Valid connected uniqueness does not distinguish those liabilities, and higher endpoint scores do not establish better synthetic plausibility. The campaign now has evidence that an earlier checkpoint can improve the reciprocal search without a reliably better valid-emission rate. Whether a more representative unlabeled diagnostic can predict that downstream usefulness remains open.

molecular_assessment.headline: Rich aryl, amine and carbonyl rings coexist with triple-bonded sulfur, nitroso groups, peroxides and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All 4,500 child trajectory rows and 4,500 corresponding Parent rows were read, including 4,350 optimizer proposals in each node. Each task supplies 900 evaluated molecules, of which 870 are optimizer proposals. The child has abundant fused heteroaromatics, saturated amine rings, aryl amides, sulfonamides and carbonyl heterocycles. Its ring-closure marker rates are 0.9816–0.9943; aromatic-marker rates are 0.7736–0.9747, with the lower value reflecting substantial unsaturated nonaromatic ring chemistry in one output set. These digest counters measure string-level presence, not atom fractions or perceived ring quality. Read-only RDKit inspection parses all 4,350 emitted child SMILES and gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 in the supplied task order. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures coexist with unusually bonded sulfur, N-nitroso substituents, peroxide bonds, highly contracted unsaturated rings and oversized assemblies. All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 392, 225, 563, 348 and 353 optimizer rows respectively, with assigned centres in none. The repertoire varies across seeds, while the upper tails repeatedly revisit a few related families. Chemistry quality is therefore mixed: ring and aromatic content are rich, but neither parseability nor high observed scores establish synthetic accessibility, stability or well-defined geometry. This assessment describes the output without attributing it to an algorithmic mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The digest leaders are medium-sized heteroaryl structures. Seed 0 links a quinoline-like ring system to a fused five/five-membered aza-ring framework; its leading variants carry N–O or N–O–N attachments and an oxygen-linked carbon triply bonded to hydrogen-bearing sulfur. The leading molecule has 25 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, three aromatic. Seed 2 also provides a more conventional methoxy/cyano-substituted partially saturated quinoline-like carboxamide and a different hydroxy-nitrile/amidine series with unsaturated carbocyclic or oxygen-containing rings. Across the full optimizer output the median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings, as in the Parent. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 577 for the child and 529 for the Parent; this counts local ring edits as distinct and is not a count of useful synthetic series. The Parent leaders included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide, indole-amide and quinoline/urea families. Rings, nitrogen and carbonyl groups are thus not missing, but the new leading families include more problematic connectivity.
liabilities: Fifty-one of 870 child proposals contain a carbon–sulfur triple bond, versus none in the corresponding Parent task. The leading C≡S–H environment and N–O–N or O–S attachments are not ordinary medicinal functional groups, and parsing supplies no stability or synthetic evidence.

The hydroxy-nitrile and unsaturated ring families include potentially sensitive local connectivity and unassigned stereocentres. Relative stability and geometry of those proposed forms are not established by the trajectory.
Ten optimizer proposals have at most three heavy atoms. Such fragments, as well as the cited large polyfunctional assembly, lose the connected arrangement seen in the favorable examples.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that preserve the favorable local aryl/nitrogen/substituent arrangement are not consistently established within the sulfur-rich leading family. A separate conventional nitrile/amide family is present, so the limitation is not an inability to make amides or nitriles.
Defined configurations are absent for substituted fused-ring and hydroxy-nitrile centres. The data do not establish which stereoisomer, if any, would be preferred.
Controlled core replacements preserving useful local functionality remain incomplete: some changes retain the core but sharply lose the score, while fragmentation removes it entirely.

applicability_conditions: This experiment requires an actual choice among unlabeled training checkpoints and variation in their valid, connected, distinct ancestral emission yields. If the loss-minimizing checkpoint already wins the molecular probe, no beneficial changed selection is assumed.

The fixed selection stream reduces arbitrary comparison noise but can itself be overfit by checkpoint selection. The independent final shared-noise audit is diagnostic only; it cannot rescue a failed result by selecting a different checkpoint.

Valid connected canonical uniqueness is a task-agnostic generative property, not a claim of synthetic accessibility, stable chemistry, medicinal quality or objective value. Rare-element and reactive high-score families and missing stereochemistry in the supplied sibling are not repaired by this selection criterion.

All raw diagnostic samples are de novo draws from the current neural checkpoint, carry no oracle labels and are discarded after counts/logs. The corpus remains used only for unlabeled training/holdout, and no fixed candidate library is introduced.

Training-only compute and checkpoint choice are distinct: the original-NLL stopping tracker and all gradient operations remain fixed, but the additional probes may still consume preparation time. approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from the original unlabeled corpus strings and retains the checkpoint with the lowest heldout token loss. Each objective clones that prior into an adaptable flow policy and keeps the reference prior frozen. The online loop alternates a neural batch with two graph batches; accepted neural molecules refresh the breeding population and provide a protected parent at the first graph handoff. Accepted-score fingerprint posterior samples choose the other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance learning of the neural policy. The same reciprocal loop is retained here. The preparation choice being questioned is its use of string likelihood alone to decide which learned prior all those components receive.
approach.novelty: Choose the prepared checkpoint by its observed yield of valid, connected, distinct molecules under a fixed ancestral sampling probe, with heldout token loss breaking ties. A separate diagnostic probe then compares that choice with the ordinary loss-minimizing checkpoint from the same training trajectory. This sibling changes checkpoint selection, whereas the previous preparation sibling changed the strings used for training. It neither combines the two interventions nor changes neural learning, graph construction or posterior allocation during an objective.

Worse online validity, chemical coverage or final task scores after a supported pure-prior yield change are negative downstream evidence; they do not establish missing selection execution.
